annotation.title_clean: Towards Trustworthy Physical Intelligence: From Theory to Practice Across the Life Cycle
annotation.title_en: Towards Trustworthy Physical Intelligence: From Theory to Practice Across the Life Cycle
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Yang, W.; Liu, H.; Xu, X.; Menon, A.; Cai, X.; He, Y.; et al.
annotation.summary_en: Survey proposing T-PAIO and T-PAI frameworks for trustworthy physical intelligence (embodied AI, robots, autonomous vehicles). It traces failure propagation, physics foundations, and operationalises governance across five life cycle stages (research, design, data, model, deployment), with quantitative safety and evidence measures.
key_provisions_or_claims: Physical AI governance extends digital AI governance via direct application, reformulation and new physical-specific elements.
Life cycle, not model, is the unit of trustworthiness; risk R(t) changes over service life, requiring continuous assurance and re-validation.
Report stage-transfer gaps (sim-to-real) and statistical evidence (Wilson intervals, rule of three) for embodied safety claims.
Latency and inference time are safety parameters in speed-and-separation monitoring design.
Logging and explanation fidelity are separate requirements; responsibility across OEM, developer, integrator and operator must be allocated at design time.
